summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain, diabetic gastroparesis, hypertension, and depression was admitted due to an acute worsening of abdominal pain, nausea, and poor oral intake. Her vital signs were stable, and physical exam revealed only mild right lower quadrant tenderness. Laboratory tests, including CBC, metabolic panel, liver enzymes, and lipase, were normal. Given her recent negative imaging and stable condition, no additional radiology was performed. She improved with IV fluids, pain control, and transition back to her oral medications, including ondansetron and metoclopramide for nausea. Her diabetes and blood pressure remained well-controlled. She was discharged home with instructions to continue her home regimen and follow up with her primary care provider, gastroenterologist, psychiatrist, and pain clinic.
